messages:

Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:15:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap + quick clarification on residency

Hi Lena — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the ask I promised: 

- Requirement summary (as I understood it): EuroFin requires EU-only data residency for customer content and logs for Phase 1 of the rollout; APAC users are out of scope for now but may come later.
- Primary question we need clarified: does "EU-only" include metadata/logging (request timestamps, anonymized latencies) or strictly content/embeddings and any KVS?
- Deployment candidates we discussed: Hosted (EU region), Dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity in EU), Private VPC/on-prem (customer-managed). A few tradeoffs we discussed: hosted is fastest to launch, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and contractual isolation, Private gives the most control for strict residency and network controls.

Next steps I propose: can you confirm whether metadata/logs need to remain in EU? If yes, we will treat Hosted as only viable if we can confirm logs & backups remain in-region (we'll surface that to infra/security). If not, Hosted EU remains simplest.

Attached: 2-page options summary I pulled together for quick read. I looped in Chloe (solutions) and Marissa (account lead). Once you confirm, Chloe can scope a short technical note comparing Dedicated vs Private for your procurement/security teams.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Hi Alex — thanks for the concise recap. Correct on Phase 1: EU-only means all customer content, embeddings, and any generated artifacts must remain in EU. 

On metadata/logging: we treat logs as sensitive if they can be linked back to customer accounts. Our legal team expects logs and telemetry that include account identifiers or request/response hashes to be stored in-region. Aggregated anonymized telemetry (totals, latency percentiles w/o account ids) can be collected out-of-region for product analytics if needed, but we'd prefer to avoid that initially.

Procurement note: procurement@eurofin.co — two asks: (1) can Redwood provide a routing guarantee that EU traffic (including backups, snapshots, and logs) will not be routed outside EU? (2) what are the options for KMS/HSM integration for customer-managed keys? Please cc security.

Lena
Head of Data Governance, EuroFin Analytics
lena.schmidt@eurofin.co

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick clarification on residency

Thanks Lena — very helpful. To answer Procurement/security at a high level (Chloe & Diego will expand):

Option A — Hosted (EU region only):
- Pros: Fastest to spin up, Redwood-managed updates, lower initial cost.
- Residency caveat: We can guarantee that primary model inference, content, and embeddings are stored and processed in the EU region. However, for our hosted service we need to validate that all backups, metrics with account identifiers, and any cross-region fallbacks are disabled or constrained. We can provide a routing SLA and an architecture diagram for EU-only flows, plus a contractual data processing addendum (DPA) that specifies in-region storage.

Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity in EU):
- Pros: Dedicated GPU pool in EU, stronger isolation, we can add contractual controls on routing and retention, and provide per-tenant logging partitions.
- Cons: longer lead time (capacity reservation), higher commit. Good middle ground if you want Redwood to operate the stack but keep stronger guarantees.

Option C — Private VPC / On-prem:
- Pros: You control network egress, KMS/HSM, and physical location — best fit for strict residency and regulatory control.
- Cons: longest lead time and higher operational overhead on your side if on-prem.

KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys (KMS integration) for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted EU, we can support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) patterns via a customer KMS tenancy in the same cloud region; Redwood will integrate via our KMS connectors but we need procurement/legal to confirm key escrow and rotation terms.

Routing guarantee & cross-region fallback: we can supply a formal routing policy that sets EU-as-primary and disables cross-region fallback for the initial contract term. If you later want APAC support, we can add region-aware routing with data residency controls.

I'll ask Diego to add the technical checklist for procurement and tag items with must-have vs nice-to-have. Chloe will scope pricing delta (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical workshop next week with EuroFin security/infra to walk the options and sign off on required controls. What days/times work for you?

Thanks —
Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick clarification on residency — technical checklist

Hi all — Diego from Redwood security/infra here. Quick technical points to help EuroFin procurement/security triage: 

1) EU-only hosted constraint (must-haves):
- Region pinned compute: we will pin inference clusters and persistent storage to eu-west-1 (or a mutually agreed EU region).
- No cross-region backups: snapshots/backups can be configured to remain in-region; we will mark cross-region replication as disabled in the deployment template.
- Logging partitions: application and request logs that contain account IDs will be written to an EU-only log bucket/cluster. Aggregated metrics are sent to global telemetry only if anonymized.

2) KMS options by deployment mode:
- Hosted EU: support BYOK via customer-managed KMS in the EU account. Redwood does not hold plaintext keys. We will require key rotation and an integration testing window.
- Dedicated: Native support for tenant KMS bindings; Redwood can perform envelope encryption with customer-provided keys.
- Private: Full customer control for on-prem HSMs.

3) SLA and contractual items:
- We can provide a routing appendix to the DPA that guarantees in-region data residency for the primary contract term (12 months).
- For strict compliance (e.g., financial audit), Private deployment or Dedicated with contractual attestations are recommended. Hosted can meet EU residency for Phase 1 if you accept BYOK + routing appendix.

I'll attach a short compliance checklist and a sample routing appendix for procurement. Happy to join the workshop.

— Diego Fernandez
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-compliance-checklist.xlsx
